rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when someone is smugly pleased after winning or seeing an opponent lose.

example.english: They were exultant after winning the match, and it was really irritating to watch.
example.traditional: 佢贏咗場比賽仲喺度得戚，真係睇到人眼冤。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jeng4 zo2 coeng4 bei2 coi3 zung6 hai2 dou6 dak1 cik1 zan1 hai6 tai2 dou2 jan4 ngaan5 jyun1

rows.note: Use this for openly exuberant, high-spirited happiness after a victory, without implying smugness.

example.english: We were exultant and sang all night after our team won the cup.
example.traditional: 我哋隊捧盃嗰晚，成班人興高采烈咁唱歌。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 deoi6 pung2 bui1 go2 maan5 seng4 baan1 jan4 hing3 gou1 coi2 lit6 gam3 coeng3 go1

rows.note: Use this specifically when the person's exultation comes from someone else's misfortune or failure.

example.english: They were exultant when their opponent lost, which was really mean.
example.traditional: 佢見到對手輸咗，竟然幸災樂禍咁笑。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gin3 dou2 deoi3 sau2 syu1 zo2 ging2 jin4 hang6 zoi1 lok6 wo6 gam3 siu3
